chest_pain_type.description: Chest pain type, ordered from no characteristic pain to asymptomatic. Ordinal code from the source dataset.

st_slope.description: Peak-exercise ST segment slope, ordered from downsloping to upsloping. Ordinal code from the source dataset.

unavailable_features.smoker: The dataset has no smoking column. The value is not fabricated and not assumed to be zero, so the model score is independent of smoking status.
unavailable_features.glucose: 'fastingbloodsugar' is a binary flag for fasting glucose above 120 mg/dL, not a glucose concentration, so it is not the same quantity as the API's 'glucose'.

dataset_only_columns.gender: Sex; not accepted by the API.
dataset_only_columns.restingrelectro: Resting ECG result; not accepted by the API.
dataset_only_columns.maxheartrate: Maximum heart rate; not accepted by the API.
dataset_only_columns.exerciseangia: Exercise-induced angina; not accepted by the API.
dataset_only_columns.oldpeak: ST depression; not accepted by the API.
dataset_only_columns.noofmajorvessels: Major vessels coloured by fluoroscopy; not accepted by the API.
dataset_only_columns.fastingbloodsugar: Binary fasting-glucose flag; not accepted by the API.

label: target
target_semantics: target = 1 means the patient is recorded as having cardiovascular disease in a cross-sectional dataset. It carries no time horizon, so the model's probability is a disease likelihood and NOT a 10-year or any other time-to-event risk estimate.

base.confidence_basis: 1000 training rows and a cross-validated ROC-AUC of 0.800: real but modest discrimination. The confidence is capped at 'moderate' because the dataset's labels are rule-derived, so the metrics cannot establish clinical validity.

extended.confidence_basis: 1000 training rows and a cross-validated ROC-AUC of 0.984. Capped at 'moderate' because the dataset's labels are rule-derived, so the metrics cannot establish clinical validity.

confidence_basis: 1000 training rows and a cross-validated ROC-AUC of 0.800: real but modest discrimination. The confidence is capped at 'moderate' because the dataset's labels are rule-derived, so the metrics cannot establish clinical validity.
limitations: The dataset's labels are rule-derived rather than observed clinical outcomes, so held-out metrics measure how well the model recovers the generating rule and do not establish clinical validity.
The target is cross-sectional: the output is a disease likelihood, not a time-to-event risk estimate, and must not be presented as a 10-year risk.
Smoking status is absent from the training data, so the model cannot account for it; the rule-based scorer does, and reports an unknown smoking status differently from a confirmed non-smoker.

The extended model needs both chest pain type and ST slope. A case that supplies only one of them is scored by the weaker base model, so the reported confidence does not depend on how the case was filled in.
The dataset still has columns the API does not accept (resting ECG, maximum heart rate, exercise angina, ST depression, vessels coloured), which carry part of the label's signal.
The dataset is small relative to clinical risk models and comes from a single source population, so performance on other populations is unknown.
